title: Demolition agreement for Kochi’s unsafe Chander Kunj Army flats signed; controlled implosion to raze twin towers by mid-April
content: Kochi: Nearly 22 months after the Kerala High Court ordered their demolition, the structurally unsafe Chander Kunj Army Towers B and C at Kochi's Vyttila have moved closer to being razed. Authorities have signed a formal agreement with Mumbai-based Edifice Engineering on November 21, setting a six-month schedule for the demolition and clearance of the site. If all goes as planned, the demolition is expected to take place in early-to-mid April 2027. The agreement was signed by Fort Kochi Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) G Sai Krishna, representing the Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) and the High Court-appointed Executive Committee headed by the Ernakulam District Collector, and Shaji Koshy, Project Manager and authorised signatory of Edifice Engineering. The contractor will demolish the two 26-storey towers at Silver Sand Island through controlled implosion, remove the debris and clear the site up to the pile caps. The agreement marks a major breakthrough in a project held up by legal challenges, contractor-selection disputes and delays in handing over the apartments. The signing came a day after owners of the 208 condemned apartments began handing over their keys to AWHO in the presence of revenue officials. Edifice has begun preliminary mobilisation, but full-fledged operations are awaiting the handover of all apartments. Sources at Edifice Engineering told Onmanorama that around 80 per cent of the flats had been handed over, with the remaining ones to be completed at the earliest. We are waiting for all the flats to be handed over. Once everyone gives us the flats, we start full-fledged, a senior official said, adding that the company could not begin demolition operations while some apartments remained under the owners' possession. The immediate priority will be to safeguard the adjoining Tower A, where 56 families continue to reside. Edifice will erect barricades, shift essential utilities, including the sewage treatment plant (STP) and transformers, and install temporary external construction lifts on Towers B and C to facilitate the movement of workers and materials. The existing 10 internal lifts will be dismantled floor by floor and handed over to AWHO, as they are excluded from the contractor's scrap rights. Our first priority is the habitability of Tower A. Firstly, we will be barricading them. Then STPs, and Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing (MEPs), which are now common for all three towers, need to be shifted just for Tower A, the official said. He said the initial salvaging work could begin in another 15-20 days, but stressed that ensuring Tower A's habitability would take precedence. The agreement provides for 24 weeks of core execution, apart from 15 days each for initial mobilisation and final demobilisation. The controlled implosion is scheduled for Week 16, which may fall in mid-April. However, Mehta said no specific blast date had been decided. The project timeline will begin after the complete handover and mobilisation. 9.66-cr contract; 6.25-crore scrap adjustment According to the agreement, the net demolition contract value is 9,66,40,689, excluding GST, after adjusting an estimated recoverable scrap value of 6,25,15,000. Edifice will retain electrical fittings, fixtures, telephone lines and fire systems on an as is where is basis. A 25 per cent mobilisation advance will be released against a 1-crore Performance Security Bank Guarantee, approved demolition methodology and insurance receipts. Another 25 per cent will be paid two weeks after the implosion, subject to PWD certification, while the remaining 50 per cent will be released after debris disposal, site handover and submission of statutory compliance certificates. The project schedule provides for structural preparation and removal of loose materials before the implosion in Week 16. The following eight weeks will be used for debris segregation and disposal, foundation and pile-cap removal, and final site clearance by Week 24...
